name: SNMP switches
author: Netlens
description: Asks managed switches (SNMP v1 / v2c, read-only) which devices are plugged into which port: the MAC address table of every switch, and LLDP (and Cisco CDP) to see how the switches are connected. Netlens then shows each device's switch and port and places the switches in the hierarchy. Works with switches that offer the standard bridge MIB (TP-Link, Netgear, HP / Aruba, Juniper, Huawei, Zyxel, MikroTik...); Cisco is read per VLAN.

config.label: Switches
config.help: Every managed switch to read. Add a port after a colon if it is not 161 (192.168.1.2:1161). A switch without its own community uses the default one below.

config.label: Default read community
config.help: The SNMP read community string you set on the switches (many ship with public). A read-only community is enough; this plugin never writes.

config.label: Core switch
config.help: Optional. The switch closest to your router, from which the others hang. Without it the switch with the most neighbours is used.

config.label: Cisco VLAN indexing

options.label: Automatic (Cisco switches without a Q-BRIDGE table)
Always (read every VLAN of every switch)

config.help: Cisco IOS keeps a separate MAC address table for every VLAN and shows only VLAN 1 to a plain community string. Netlens then asks for each VLAN with community@vlan. Leave it on Automatic unless the diagnostic shows a switch whose devices are missing.

config.label: Timeout per request (seconds)
config.help: How long to wait for an answer before asking again (twice). Raise it for slow switches.
